title: Brussels march against COVID-19 restrictions by Ensemble pour la liberté
location: March from Brussels North Station toward the European Quarter
scope: Local Brussels march, organized by a coalition; no wider national network of simultaneous events is established by the opened source.
organizer: Ensemble pour la liberté (“Together for Freedom”), bringing together several associations
participants_original: Le Point/AFP reports thousands; police estimated 5,000.
threshold_50_evidence: The opened AFP report attributes an estimate of 5,000 participants to police, clearly above the 50-person threshold; this is a reported estimate, not an exact count.

occurrence.summary: The opened AFP report describes thousands marching in Brussels on Sunday 9 January 2022.

start_date.summary: The article dates the march to Sunday 9 January 2022.

end_date.summary: The report dates the march to Sunday 9 January and says police detained about 30 people after the march; it does not give a closing time. The separate 11 preventive arrests occurred before the march and do not establish its end.

location.summary: The march ran from Brussels North Station toward the European Quarter.

scope.summary: The observed event was a local Brussels march organized by a coalition; no other simultaneous sites are described in this opened report.

organizer.summary: The call came from Ensemble pour la liberté, which the report says brought together several associations.

demands.summary: Participants opposed the health pass and pandemic restrictions; signs opposed a vaccine mandate and vaccination of children, directed at Belgian policy.

participants_original.summary: The AFP report describes thousands, with a police estimate of 5,000.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The police estimate of 5,000 supports that the public gathering exceeded 50, while retaining the estimate as approximate.

protester_violence.summary: The report says a small group threw projectiles near European institutions; this does not characterize the whole march.

state_response.summary: Police pushed back a small group that threw projectiles and reported about 30 detentions after the march. Separately, 11 preventive arrests were made before it for pyrotechnics and inflammable material. The report does not describe beatings, shootings, killings, a negotiated concession or government inaction.

notes: Le Point carries AFP copy; treat syndicated AFP material as one origin. A Belga photo credit does not make the report a Belga-origin confirmation. The article’s ministerial call for parliamentary debate is not established as a response to the march or as a concession. Detentions after the march and 11 preventive arrests before it are distinct; the physical closing time is unstated.
open_questions: The physical closing time is unknown, although the source places the reported post-march detentions after the same-day march.
Local or official turnout corroboration and independent confirmation of the organizer would improve evidence diversity.

title: Brussels demonstration against COVID-19 measures
location: March from Brussels North Station to Cinquantenaire/Jubelpark
scope: One organized Brussels march with participants from Belgium and abroad. VRT says police announced the demonstration over at about 15:00; a few hundred rioters then continued, so that announcement is not treated as the physical end of all assembly.
participants_original: VRT reports approximately 50,000 participants from Belgium and abroad.
threshold_50_evidence: The opened VRT report estimates approximately 50,000 participants, clearly above 50; this is a reported estimate rather than an exact count.

occurrence.summary: VRT describes a Brussels demonstration and march on 23 January 2022.

start_date.summary: VRT dates the demonstration to 23 January 2022.

end_date.summary: VRT says police announced around 15:00 that the demonstration had ended; it then describes a few hundred people continuing in disorder. The date is same-day, but the 15:00 announcement is not treated as the physical end of all assembly.

location.summary: The march began at Brussels North Station and ended at Cinquantenaire/Jubelpark.

scope.summary: VRT reports participants from Belgium and abroad and describes one Brussels march; a few hundred then continued in a distinct violent subgroup.

demands.summary: Participants opposed coronavirus measures; the article mentions opposition to the COVID pass and vaccination of children.

participants_original.summary: VRT reports approximately 50,000 participants from Belgium and abroad.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The approximately 50,000 estimate clearly exceeds the 50-person threshold.

protester_violence.summary: The report describes a few hundred people damaging property and confronting police after the main march; this violence is not attributed to all marchers.

state_response.summary: Police dispersed the continuing group and 228 people were arrested, 11 judicially detained. These response details concern the post-march subgroup; the article does not establish beatings, shootings, killings, concessions or ignoring.

notes: The organized march and its violent aftermath are temporally linked in the source but have distinct phases. Do not use the few-hundred rioters as a separate turnout estimate or the 228 arrests as crowd size. Statements that offenders would be prosecuted do not establish accommodation. Organizer is not identified in the opened body text used here.
open_questions: Exact physical end time of the full assembly and later subgroup is not established.
The source does not allocate the 12 non-officer injuries by cause; independent primary or local corroboration would improve response coding.
Search-only RTBF and municipal records may add context but are not coding evidence until their bodies are reviewed.
